subject: Contract redline: encrypted-key access & subprocessor clarification
messages:
From: Morgan Bell <morgan.bell@acmehealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme DPA - requested redlines & two clarifications

Aditya / Redwood team,

Attached is our latest redline to the DPA (Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx). Two items came up on our side that we'd like your team to confirm before legal will sign:

1) Section 4.2 (Subprocessors) — we saw a note about an analytics subprocessor that may be added for telemetry aggregation. We need a written confirmation of the specific vendor (name + country) and export-control assurances.

2) Section 6.1 (Customer data access) — there's a new clause requesting that Redwood engineers may access encrypted KV cache snapshots to help with debugging. For regulated data we need to understand: who holds the keys, under what conditions access is allowed, and whether that access triggers additional auditing or breach-notification obligations.

Can you please route to Product & Security for quick confirmation? We're on an expedited timeline — ideal to have language/confirmation by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Morgan Bell
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (docx)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Acme DPA - requested redlines & two clarifications

Morgan — thanks for the redline and the clear callouts. Looping in Product (Laura), Security (Hannah) and Infra (Dev) to confirm.

Quick context from our side:
- The telemetry subprocessor is a proposed analytics partner (we'll provide the legal name + country; tentative: DataSight Inc., EU). It's currently optional and only used for aggregated metrics — we can gate on an opt-in or disallow for Acme if required.
- Encrypted KV cache snapshots are only used for debugging time-limited inference regressions. Keys are customer-managed for Private deployments; for Hosted we currently manage keys through our KMS with strict access controls.

Requests for Product/Security:
- Product: can you propose alternate language that limits access to KV cache snapshots to time-bounded, consented debug sessions and requires redaction of PHI?
- Security/Privacy: what controls (HSM, audit logs, escalation approvals) must be added to make this acceptable?

Morgan — we'll aim to return suggested language by EOD Monday. If you need a call sooner, suggest Mon 10–11am PT.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 14 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - requested redlines & two clarifications

Thanks for the ping — quick Product take from a product-risk / customer-experience angle.

High-level: we are willing to accept a narrow, auditable debug access path for KV cache snapshots under these constraints:
- Access is explicitly time-limited (max 6 hours per incident) and tied to a named ticket ID.
- Access requires: (a) Acme engineer approval OR documented consent via the Console; and (b) two-person internal approval for hosted accounts.
- Any PII/PHI must be redacted automatically before snapshots are made available to engineering. If redaction isn't possible, we should disallow access for those keys.
- For Private (customer-managed keys), we recommend rejecting any clause that allows Redwood to possess keys — debugging is performed on customer premises or via a support container with access-controlled key escrow only.

I've attached a short PRD-snippet with suggested wording (PRD-proposed-language-encrypted-key-access.txt). If Security is comfortable with audit requirements below, we can propose this back to Acme.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Serving
Redwood Inference
Attachment: PRD-proposed-language-encrypted-key-access.txt
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Morgan Bell <morgan.bell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Jan 2027 09:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - requested redlines & two clarifications

Appreciate the notes — Security's position summarized below. I copied key controls we require to accept any language that grants Redwood engineer access to encrypted artifacts: 

Mandatory controls for hosted accounts (minimum):
- Keys: keys must be under an HSM-backed KMS; any access must be performed through a short-lived cryptographic token issued by the KMS, not by exporting keys.
- Approval flow: two approvers (Support lead + Security reviewer) and a written ticket with business justification; escalations retained for 7 years in our audit log.
- Auditability: immutable logs with proof of access (who, when, reason) and periodic audit reports shared with customer on request.
- Data minimization & redaction: automated PII/PHI scrubbing before any engineer sees snapshot. If scrubbing cannot be guaranteed for a particular snapshot, access must be denied.
- For any cross-border subprocessor (DataSight Inc. or similar), we need the vendor's SOC 2 Type II and EU SCCs if data crosses regions.

We can accept language similar to Laura's PRD text if the contract reflects these controls and we get a 30-day review period after deployment of any new subprocessor.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Morgan Bell <morgan.bell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - requested redlines & two clarifications

Morgan — summary and next steps:

1) Subprocessor: DataSight Inc. (EU) is the proposed analytics vendor. Per Security, we will only add them after they've provided SOC2 Type II evidence and agreed to SCCs. We will add a 30-day review hold in the contract for any future subprocessor additions.

2) Encrypted KV cache access: Product + Security propose the language in PRD-proposed-language-encrypted-key-access.txt with the following binding requirements: HSM-backed KMS, two-approver flow, immutable audit logs, automated PII/PHI redaction, and explicit customer consent via Console or written approval. For Private deployments, Redwood will not hold customer keys; debugging will rely on customer-managed key escrow processes.

I'll consolidate the suggested redline and return a marked-up DPA by Monday morning. Can we lock a 30-minute call Mon 10:00am PT to confirm final language? If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
